conventions.origin: on the ground (y = 0) under the model centre
conventions.bounds: [length along Z, width along X, height along Y] of the axis-aligned box, metres
conventions.left: +X is the model's left when it faces +Z (glTF convention); wheel_?l are at +X
conventions.ports: empty nodes on the 4 m cell boundary at y = 1.5; the node's +Z points out of the module and +Y is up. port_n = +Z, port_e = +X, port_s = -Z, port_w = -X (a second port on the same side is port_n2 ...). To snap B onto A: B.port world frame = A.port world frame rotated 180 deg about the port's Y axis. type "pressurized" has a docking collar and a hatch node hatch_<dir> (hide both hatches when joined); "utility" is a grid snap only; "exterior" is a walk-out door; "stack" (port_up, +Z up) takes the upper module's origin; "rover_dock" is the crew rover hatch (2.0 m high: not level with base ports).
conventions.wheels: each wheel is its own node, a direct child of the root, origin at the wheel centre, axle = local +X. Spin = rotation about X, steer = rotation about Y: in three.js node.rotation.set(spin, steer, 0, "YXZ"). Suspension travel = move node.position.y. All six wheels share one mesh per side (instanced).
conventions.materials: parts are split by named material (hull, hull_alt, trim, dark, accent, metal, glass, glass_dark, solar, tyre, glow, glow_red, regolith, rock, plant, id_blue, id_green, fabric); same name = same look across the kit. "glow*" carry emissiveFactor; "glass" is alphaMode BLEND and double sided.
conventions.triangles: rendered triangles (instanced meshes counted once per instance)
conventions.gameplay: suggested stats; each block's "notes" says which numbers are real figures and which are game design values

items.description: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 rover at real scale (3.0 x 2.7 x 2.2 m class). Six wheels are separate nodes (one decimated source wheel, instanced and mirrored); body, arm, mast and suspension are one static node.

items.processing: Draco-decoded; animations/skin dropped; wheels split out of the single Wheels_objs mesh by position, front-left wheel decimated to 27% and instanced x6 (mirrored for the right side); body parts quadric-decimated (about 131k -> 21k); large textured parts flattened to the mean colour of their texture before decimation, small textured parts (decals, plates) kept with UVs and 256 px JPEG textures; metalness capped.

gameplay.notes: Real figures: mass 1025 kg; MMRTG ~110 W electrical at start of mission; two 43 Ah Li-ion batteries (~2.4 kWh at 28 V); top speed 152 m/h = 0.042 m/s on flat hard ground. A game will want a far higher speed: suggested game design value top_speed_game_ms = 1.5.

items.processing: Print-plate shells separated by connected components and re-assembled by script: rocker-bogies turned over and hung on the hull pivot stubs, mast sunk into the deck, arm links posed in a vertical plane; print brims removed and a belly plate generated in their place; hub brackets between suspension posts and wheels are GENERATED geometry; wheel decimated 58k -> 3.6k triangles and instanced x6; materials assigned by rule (STL has none).

items.name: Astronaut (EVA suit)
items.description: NASA low-poly EVA-suited astronaut, 1.88 m. UNRIGGED: no skeleton or skin weights. The single suit mesh was cut by planes into six rigid nodes (torso > head, arm_l, arm_r, leg_l, leg_r) pivoted at the neck, shoulders and hips so a walk can be faked by swinging limbs about local X. The source is in a T-pose; the arm nodes carry a default rotation of -/+72 deg about Z that lowers them to the sides.

animation_hint.three_js: arm.rotation.set(swing, 0, restZ) with default XYZ order; leg.rotation.x = swing; walk: legs +/-25 deg, arms -/+15 deg, opposite phase

items.license: NASA media usage guidelines (https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/): generally not copyrighted, free to use; no implied NASA endorsement; NASA insignia/logotype use is restricted
items.attribution: Astronaut: model courtesy NASA, from NASA 3D Resources (https://github.com/nasa/NASA-3D-Resources); adapted (decimated / re-materialed / re-rooted) for this game. Use does not imply NASA endorsement.
items.processing: Draco-decoded; scaled to 1.88 m; suit shell clipped by 5 planes into 6 rigid parts with fan caps on the cuts; texture resized 1024 -> 512 px JPEG. Chosen over the Mark III (69k tris, inside-out torso faces, arms forward) and the Z2 (17 MB of baked 4K textures, arms-down pose that does not cut cleanly).

gameplay.notes: Real figures: a crew member consumes ~0.84 kg O2 and ~3 L drinking water per day (NASA ECLSS planning numbers); EMU primary life support lasts ~8 h. mass_kg (astronaut 80 kg + suit 120 kg) and walk speed are game design values.
